sections.html:
The courthouse at 400 N. Main Street, Salem, MO 65560 holds most of the offices you will deal with.

  • Assessor: 573-729-6010, dentcountyassessor@gmail.com. Weekday hours are 8:00 to 4:30, with major holidays off.
  • Collector of Revenue: 573-729-3911, same hours.
  • County Clerk: 573-729-4144. The Clerk schedules Board of Equalization appointments.
  • Recorder of Deeds: 112 E. Fifth Street, Suite 2, 573-729-2198.

The Assessor values taxable property. The Collector bills it, receives payment, passes the money to the taxing districts and also handles escrow payments sent in by mortgage holders. View and pay statements at dentcountycollector.com. The Assessor's GIS map pulls up a parcel by street address, owner or parcel number, and a yearly subscription is available for people who need property data or maps regularly.

Vehicle owners should know that new plates require proof that the previous year's personal property tax was paid, shown by a paid receipt or a waiver from the Assessor. The Collector also takes county merchant license fees and sends the paid personal property list to the License Bureau each month.

sections.h2: When bills go out and when tax is due
sections.html:
The Collector sends real estate and personal property bills by November 8. They are due by the end of December, and a penalty kicks in on January 1. The money is then split among 22 political subdivisions that hold certified levies, among them schools, roads and fire districts. The Collector also bills tax on state assessed utilities such as railroads, pipelines and electric lines.

  • Paying before the new year avoids the penalty, and the Collector can show you the late schedule.
  • With a lender escrowing your tax, confirm the lender really got the bill.
  • Personal property has a separate schedule. Owners list it with the Assessor between January 1 and March 1, and lateness can cost up to $105.00 under RSMo 137.280.
  • Newcomers from another Missouri county bring their last paid personal property receipt to open a Dent County account, and anyone new to the state must open one too.

After a sale, either you or the title company should report the buyer's name and mailing address to the Collector, so the next statement is not mailed to you.

The statutory assessment date is January 1, and more than 11,000 parcels are valued as of that day. Real estate falls into three subclasses: residential at 19% of market value, agricultural at 12% of production value and everything else at 32% of true value in money. A full reassessment lands in odd-numbered years, and new construction or additions are added each year.

To get the tax, divide the assessed figure by 100 and multiply by the combined levy of the districts over your parcel. Either office can look that levy up.

Your first call should be to the Assessor, to learn how the value was reached. The State Tax Commission oversees assessors, and its field representatives visit Dent County monthly and spot-review properties each year. Not convinced? The Board of Equalization is next, and RSMo 137.275 closes filing on the second Monday in July.

Hearings are booked through the County Clerk. Under RSMo 138.060 the board rules summarily, and the assessor's valuation gets no presumption of being right. If your valuation rose 15% or more over the last assessment for reasons other than new construction or improvements, the assessor must show the value is not above true market value. Bring last cycle's notice, photos and any appraisal or sales evidence.

After that, RSMo 138.430 sends you to the State Tax Commission. You have 30 days from the board's final action or until the chapter's own deadline, whichever is later, and because the right flows from the board's decision, the board hearing has to happen first.

sections.h2: Unpaid tax and the August land sale
sections.html:
The whole state auctions delinquent land on the same day, the fourth Monday in August (RSMo 140.150). An owner can head it off by paying the Dent County Collector the tax with penalty, interest and costs. For the current list and amounts, call 573-729-3911.

  • Before the list is published, a first class notice goes to the owner of public record.
  • Certified mail is used for a second notice only if assessed valuation is over $1,000.
  • A certified notice returned unsigned is followed by a first class mailing to the owner of record and to the occupant.
  • Not receiving any notice does not cancel the tax.

RSMo 140.405 requires a tax sale buyer to warn owners and lienholders of the right to redeem at least ninety days before taking a deed. Anyone holding an inherited or vacant house should call the Collector early and learn what is owed.

Here is a sensible order for a Dent County sale. Check the owner name and parcel on the Assessor's GIS map. Ask the Collector for the balance with any penalty and interest. Hand that figure to the title company so the payoff is in the settlement statement. Once the deed records, send the Collector the buyer's name and mailing address. A short list like this keeps the closing date from slipping over a tax question.

Salem is the county seat and Bunker is the other city. The county's 2020 census count was 14,421, down from 15,657 ten years earlier.

Before you list, ask the Collector for the balance on your parcel and make sure the owner name matches your deed. If tax is owed, the title company can pay it from your proceeds at closing, and the Collector only needs the new owner's mailing address afterward. A house inherited from a relative, or one left vacant, is the case where back taxes most often go unnoticed, so check it first.

Cash Home Buyers can buy such a house as it stands, with the closing agent clearing delinquent tax from the price. That skips a lender's appraisal and repair list. Ask a local title company about recent sales near you before you decide on a price, and keep your latest tax statement handy so buyers can see the annual cost for themselves.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Dent County tax without penalty?
faqs.a: The end of December. Bills go out by November 8 and the penalty begins January 1. Phone 573-729-3911 if yours is missing.

faqs.q: Can Dent County taxes be paid on the web?
faqs.a: Yes, through dentcountycollector.com, where statements can be viewed and paid. The office at 400 N. Main Street in Salem also takes payment on weekdays during business hours.

At 19% of market value. Farm ground is assessed at 12% of production value and all other property at 32% of true value in money. Full reassessment comes in odd-numbered years, with new construction added every year.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff for an appeal to the local board?
faqs.a: By the second Monday in July under RSMo 137.275. Reach the County Clerk at 573-729-4144 about hearing dates.

faqs.q: When is the personal property list due?
faqs.a: March 1. Property held on January 1 is listed with the Assessor between January 1 and March 1, and a late list can draw a penalty of up to $105.00. Newcomers must set up an account.
